title: Kernel-aware online bucketization for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Priya Anand
description: Design and implement an online, kernel-aware dynamic bucketization algorithm that groups incoming requests by both effective sequence-length and the GPU kernel profile most efficient for that request shape. The goal is to reduce padding during micro-batching while keeping GPU utilization high and meeting latency SLOs across prefill and decode phases.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrated into the continuous-batching pipeline and togglable via config flag
Validated against synthetic and production-like trace with >=10% reduction in average per-token padding overhead for mixed-seqlen chat workload
99th percentile latency for small requests does not regress by more than 5% under baseline load
End-to-end integration tests for prefill/decode handoff and KV cache consistency pass in CI
Documentation and rollout playbook added to runtime-runbook (Confluence)
milestones: M1: Design doc + kernel profiling matrix (due 2025-01-19)
M2: Controlled prototype that exposes bucket selector (due 2025-01-31)
M3: Extended prefill/decode scheduler with hybrid batching policy (due 2025-02-12)

design_decisions: Use a lightweight online histogram + LRU window to approximate current seqlen distribution instead of per-request clustering to keep selector O(1)
Expose a kernel affinity map (kernel_id -> preferred seqlen ranges) derived from offline microbenchmarks; scheduler uses affinity to bias grouping
Separate prefill and decode bucket pools: prefill buckets prioritize throughput (larger groups) whereas decode buckets prioritize latency (smaller, time-bounded groups)
When kernel affinity conflicts with latency SLO, prefer lower-padding option up to a soft latency budget; provide fallback to fastest kernel to honor SLOs
KV cache partitioning kept intact by tagging batches with canonical request IDs; no cross-batch KV-sharing introduced in prototype
implementation_notes: Added bucket_selector component under serving/batching with a pluggable policy interface
Kernel profiling tool extended to emit (kernel_id, seqlen_range, tokens/s, mem_bytes) tuples stored in runtime-config
Scheduler supports time-bound wait thresholds for decode buckets: max_wait_ms configurable per bucket-size and priority
Metrics emitted: bucket_fill_ratio, avg_padding_tokens_per_batch, kernel_affinity_mismatch_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency by bucket
experiments_and_results: Local microbench with MPT-7B-like model: 18% reduction in padding tokens, 9% end-to-end token cost drop for mixed chat traces
Staging A/B on region-us-east with replayed week-of-traffic: 12% median pad reduction, 11% tail-latency improvement for medium-length queries (seqlen 64-512)
Worst-case small-request latency increased by 3.2% at 95th under best-effort throughput policy; within acceptance criteria
Kernel switching overhead measured at ~0.4ms per switch due to kernel warm/cache; scheduler penalizes frequent switches via hysteresis
tradeoffs_and_risks: More complex selector increases code surface for the hot-path — mitigated by keeping selection code lockfree and small
Kernel affinity map staleness risk when models or quantization change — mitigated by CI job that re-profiles kernels on model onboarding
Potential KV cache fragmentation if buckets become too specialized; we limit number of active bucket types to reduce fragmentation
Rolling out without good observability could cause transient regressions in tail latency — mitigate with staged rollout and automated rollback policy
